summary:
Field Shift — Adapting Farms with NASA Data

Field Shift is a bilingual, voice-enabled farming assistant designed to make climate information more accessible and understandable for farmers, particularly those who are not comfortable using English or complex digital tools. Developed with a focus on Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh, our prototype integrates NASA POWER data to present rainfall and temperature information through a simple climate dashboard.

Farmers can interact with the assistant in English or Telugu, ask voice-based questions about annual and monthly rainfall and temperature, and receive spoken responses. A monthly rainfall chart helps users identify variations in rainfall throughout the year. The Crop Rotation Explorer also presents locally relevant options, including paddy followed by blackgram and paddy followed by greengram, with suitability depending on local field conditions.

By combining NASA Earth data, regional-language accessibility and agricultural information in one platform, Field Shift aims to bridge the gap between climate data and farmers' understanding , supporting more informed agricultural decisions.
details: Field Shift — Adapting Farms with NASA Data Field Shift is a bilingual, voice-enabled farming assistant designed to make climate information more accessible and understandable for farmers, especially those who may not be comfortable with English or complex digital tools. Our prototype focuses on Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh, India. It integrates climate information from NASA POWER, including daily precipitation and temperature data for 2025 at a representative location near Machilipatnam. This information is presented through a simple climate dashboard displaying average temperature, total rainfall, and a monthly rainfall chart. One of the key features of Field Shift is its voice-based question-answering system. Farmers can interact with the assistant in English or Telugu, ask questions about rainfall, temperature, and crop rotation, and receive spoken responses in their selected language. This makes climate information easier to access without requiring users to navigate complicated charts or understand technical terminology. The Crop Rotation Explorer presents locally relevant examples, including paddy followed by blackgram (వరి → మినుములు) and paddy followed by greengram (వరి → పెసలు). These options are intended as informative suggestions; actual crop suitability depends on soil conditions, water availability, sowing time, and local agricultural guidance. We developed Field Shift using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Chart.js is used to create the rainfall visualization, while the NASA POWER API provides climate data. Browser-based Speech Recognition and Speech Synthesis technologies support voice input and spoken responses in English and Telugu. The prototype is designed as a lightweight web application that can be accessed through a browser. The creative aspect of Field Shift is the combination of NASA Earth data, regional-language interaction, voice accessibility, climate visualization, and agricultural information in a single platform. Instead of presenting raw climate datasets, it helps users explore and understand the information through familiar language and simple interactions. During development, we considered the needs of farmers, language accessibility, ease of use, regional agricultural relevance, data clarity, and the limitations of available climate information. We also recognized that a representative location's data should not be interpreted as an exact measurement for every part of the district. Our intended impact is to bridge the gap between satellite-based climate information and farming communities. Field Shift aims to help farmers better understand rainfall and temperature patterns, explore possible crop-rotation choices, and make more informed agricultural decisions with accessible climate information.
projectRefs: Web Speech API – Speech Recognition and Speech Synthesis
